use_case: Predictive maintenance model for well equipment: predicts rod pump and ESP failures up to 30 days ahead from historian and work order data, to prioritize well servicing rigs
vendor_or_model: Company-owned gradient-boosted classification model built by 2 production data engineers with a contracted data science firm on the cloud ML workspace
data_categories: Historian data from the cloud replica (pump cards, motor current, runtime, pressures, rates); ERP work order history with technician names removed; no personal information
consequential_decision_category: None (equipment); re-tier to Safety/CI if outputs ever act on equipment or defer safety-critical inspections, and to Employment if used to evaluate staff
human_in_the_loop: A production engineer reviews every alert and decides whether to create a work order; dismissals need a reason; no write path to SCADA or the ERP
applicable_laws: No sector AI rule; FTC Act Section 5 for the company's own claims about the model; contract terms with the data science firm (data use, ownership, deletion); Fla. Stat. 501.171 not triggered because no personal information is used
status: In production since 2026-03 in the Panhandle and Alabama (about 310 wells); South Florida (about 110 wells) in shadow mode until the bias threshold is met

use_case: Enterprise generative AI assistant in the productivity suite: drafts, summarizes, and searches documents and email for 300 licensed users
vendor_or_model: Productivity suite vendor's generative AI assistant (large language model) under enterprise terms
data_categories: Any file or message the user can open, including Restricted data in over-shared folders (owner deck exports, seismic interpretations, OT diagrams)
human_in_the_loop: Users review every output; outputs are never used in filings, notices, or owner, shipper, or partner communications without checking the source
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) (reasonable measures for personal information it can reach); trade secret protection for seismic and reservoir data; license terms prohibit training on company data; NIST AI 600-1 risks (confabulation, information security, data privacy)
status: In production since 2026-02 for 300 users; expansion paused until over-shared folders are fixed (2026-11-30) and labels applied (2026-12-31)

use_case: Gathering line leak analytics: flags possible leaks on the 14-mile trunk line and 3 metered laterals from real-time pressure and flow patterns, as advisory alerts on OCC HMIs
vendor_or_model: SCADA historian vendor's leak analytics add-on (statistical and machine learning model), installed on the OCC historian
data_categories: Real-time pressure, flow, and temperature data from the SCADA historian; no personal information
human_in_the_loop: Advisory only: never clears or suppresses an alarm; controllers record a reason for every dismissal; monthly dismissed-alert review; pressure and flow alarms, line riders, and the pipeline emergency procedures remain primary
applicable_laws: Voluntary tool: 49 CFR 195.11(b) does not list leak detection for regulated rural gathering lines, and the tool is not used to meet any Part 195 duty; the 1-hour notice under 49 CFR 195.52 is unaffected; FTC Act Section 5 for claims made to shippers
status: In production since 2026-04; controller procedure due 2026-10-31 and training due 2026-11-30

use_case: HR candidate-screening feature: ranks applicants for field roles by resume match
vendor_or_model: HR and payroll SaaS vendor's AI screening feature (machine learning ranking model)
data_categories: Resumes and application answers (personal information of about 1,100 applicants a year)
human_in_the_loop: Feature is switched off. If ever enabled: a recruiter reviews every application and no applicant is rejected by the tool alone
applicable_laws: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act (42 U.S.C. 2000e-2); Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR 1607.4: impact records and the four-fifths rule); state AI employment laws if hiring in a covered state (for example Colorado SB26-189, effective 2027-01-01); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)
status: Licensed 2025-11; switched off with a feature-change alert; not approved (risk avoided, P01 R-034); decision point 2027-03-31

use_case: ERP invoice coding: suggests general ledger account, cost center, and AFE for vendor invoices
vendor_or_model: ERP SaaS vendor's invoice coding feature (classification on the company's coding history)
data_categories: Vendor invoices and coding history; vendor names and addresses
human_in_the_loop: A payables clerk approves every coding; the invoice approval workflow is unchanged
applicable_laws: Contract terms with the ERP vendor (confirm no training on company data); joint operating agreements (accurate partner billing)
status: In production since 2026-05; monthly 50-invoice accuracy sample
